font.$description: The type ROLES — the surface a spoke re-points. These were tier-1 primitives until the tier-1 typography audit: `--font-sans` names a classification rather than a face, and type-roles.css documents it as the spoke's override surface, which made the shipped contract an instruction to re-point a primitive. The names are unchanged, so every reader kept working; only the tier moved. NOTE: a `$description` at the ROOT of a semantic file collides with the one in effect.json — Style Dictionary merges file roots — so group level is the right home for it.

sans.$description: The body face. A spoke re-points this to its brand face.

display.$description: Headline/display face. Defaults to the body face (zero visual change) so the slot exists for a spoke to override with a distinct face — e.g. a condensed family for logotypes and big numbers. Wired into the display/title type-roles.

font-weight.$description: Weight ROLES. The numbers are typeface-bound — 350/500/550/650 are DM Sans's optical weights, not universal values — so a spoke swapping the body face re-points these to that face's matching weights. That is exactly why they are roles at tier 2 and the raw numbers are the primitives at tier 1.

font-size-ui.$description: Text inside interface furniture — control labels, table headers, pills, pagination. Deliberately aligned step-for-step with --control-height-*, so a component rendered at size `md` reads --font-size-ui-md. Prose keeps using the type-roles in type-roles.css; this ramp is for chrome, not content.
